newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's new army chief wants to cut troops.
newsitem.headline: Poland's new army chief wants to cut troops.

text.p: Poland wants to reduce the number of troops in its armed forces to save money needed for modernisation, the country's new chief of staff Henryk Szumski said on Wednesday.
Szumski said that he aims to reduce Poland's troops by 40,000 to 180,000 within seven years, television news reported.
"Our regiments are spread out over many garrisons, which causes substantial costs and our ability to finance training does not meet our needs," Szumski said.
A detailed plan of the Polish army's reform should be accepted by a government tast-force chaired by Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz by the end of May, the television said.
